summary: Dungkar Lobsang Thrinle (1927–1997) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Trashichöling, Sera, and Gyuto monasteries under Ngawang Yönten and Tsadru Ngawang Losang. He held posts at Minzu University, Tibet University, and the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences.

Durga Mohan Bhattacharyya (1899–1965) was an Indologist educated at Vidyasagar College, Scottish Church College, and the University of Calcutta. He served as a professor at Narasinha Dutt College, Scottish Church College, and the Sanskrit College and University.

Durga Prasad Dikshit is a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He earned his PhD at the University of Lucknow, studying under doctoral supervisor Baij Nath Puri and teachers R. K. Dikshit and Vasudev Vishnu Mirashi.

Dwarikadas Shastri (b. 1922) works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He earned the Bauddhadarśanācārya at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, founded Bauddha Bharati, and served as joint editor (सहसम्पादक) at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara.

Dwijendra Narayan Jha (1940–2021) was an Indology, history, and archaeology scholar who completed his studies at Patna University, Presidency University (~1957–1959), and the University of Calcutta (~1960–1964).
Dylan Esler is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at SOAS University of London and completed his PhD at KU Leuven in 2018, where he also served as a research scholar.

Dzigar Kongtrul Rinpoche (b. 1964) is a scholar in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. He studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Nyoshul Khenpo, Tulku Urgyen, and Khenpo Rinchen, founded Mangala Shri Bhuti, and taught at Naropa University in 1990.

Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche (b. 1965) is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar educated at Karma Shri Nalanda Institute, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and Columbia University. He directed Kamalashila Institute (~1992) and founded the Nitartha Institute, Nitartha International, and Nalandabodhi.

Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse Rinpoche (b. 1961) is a Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies scholar educated at Sakya College and SOAS. He studied under teachers including Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and founded Siddhartha's Intent, Khyentse Foundation, and Deer Park Institute.
Dániel Balogh works in Indology, linguistics, and history/archaeology. He has held positions at the British Museum (attested 2021) and Eötvös Loránd University (attested 2026).

Dörte Kamarid is a Tibetology and Indology scholar who studied at Savitribai Phule Pune University, the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, and the University of Vienna, where she completed a BA and studied under MA supervisor Helmut Tauscher.
E. Easwaran Nampoothiry (b. 1930) is an Indologist who studied under S. Venkitasubramonia Iyer and served as a lecturer in the Sanskrit Department at the University of Kerala (attested 1973).

E. F. Schumacher (1911–1977) was a philosopher who studied under Edward Conze and attended the University of Bonn, New College, Columbia University, and the LSE. He held academic posts at Columbia University (~1931–1932) and the University of Oxford.

E. Gene Smith (1936–2010) was a Tibetologist who studied at Adelphi, Hobart and William Smith, Utah, and Washington under Turrell V. Wylie. He worked at the Library of Congress and founded and directed the Buddhist Digital Resource Center.

E. Michael Mendelson (1928–2024) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar who was educated at King's College, Cambridge, the University of Cambridge, the University of Paris, and the University of Chicago.
E. R. Sreekrishna Sarma (1922–1994) was an Indology and philosophy scholar who earned his PhD from the University of Marburg in 1954 and held a post at Sri Venkateswara University (attested 1977).

E. W. Adikaram (1905–1985) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Wesley College, the University of Colombo, SOAS, and the University of London under William Stede. In 1934, he became principal of Ananda Sastralaya, Kotte.

Eberhard Fischer (b. 1941) is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who earned his PhD from the University of Basel in 1965. He served as director of Museum Rietberg (1972–1998) and held posts at the Rietberg-Gesellschaft and SLSA.

Eberhard Sandschneider (b. 1955) is a Sinologist who earned his PhD at Saarland University. He held positions at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (1995–1998), Free University of Berlin (1999–2001), and the German Council on Foreign Relations (2003–2016).

Eberhard Schrader (1836–1908) was a scholar in linguistics who studied under Heinrich Ewald at the University of Göttingen. He held professorial posts at the universities of Zurich, Giessen, Jena, and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1875–1908).
